title: Bounded Lungro received-language evidence and local Greek/Italo-Albanian calendar components

integration.required_correction: GR-INT-001: all nine disposable research_artifact_path fields removed from added and updated source tables, including three inherited paths. Exact source hashes, sizes, URLs and limits retained.

semantics: Concrete local received-language and calendar/rubric evidence found; no blanket Church adoption, full receiving celebrant book, whole-book transcription, collation, historical transition or ancestry asserted.

findings.assertion: Official 2015 bulletin names Liturgjia Hyjnore e atit tonë ndër shëjtrat Joan Hrysostomit and expressly says it remains in use in Lungro Arbëresh parishes. The bishop’s 2018 pastoral identifies Congregation approval and reports Albanian commonly used in almost all parishes. Candidate byzantine-greek-lungro1968 should no longer be automatically deferred solely as translation.
findings.limit: The physical book was not acquired; 1967/1968 printing, press and bilingual-format reports differ. No reception outside Lungro inferred.

findings.assertion: 2023 retrospective says decree published 6 August 1968; 2018 pastoral says adoption decreed 13 October 1968. Both point to Bollettino 3 (1968), pp. 14–16. 2014 quotes Assembly art.120 requiring Albanian/Greek, with Italian in Italophone parishes or elsewhere by ordinary permission.
findings.limit: Preserve attributed dates; do not assert that October is independently proven implementation date. Original decree and Assembly act remain uninspected. 2023 quote itself prints con where sense appears non; no silent repair or reliance on that malformed phrase.

findings.assertion: Official 20 January announcement says this Ordo was already circulated to regulate festive and daily Vespers, Orthros, Hours and Divine Liturgy. Primary PDF p.60 assigns Pascha 5 April 2026 and Chrysostom with propers/readings.
findings.limit: One local calendar/rubric component. No full-book adoption, new recension, first celebration or full implementation claimed. Piana appendix credit does not rename the whole book.

support: piana-imerologhion2019.pdf, original cover PDF p.1, credits p.3, Note per l’uso p.10/printed p.11
findings.assertion: Piana Curia/Ufficio Liturgico’s own Ordo names Roman Greek Anthologion 1967–1980 and Lipa Italian 1999–2000. It explicitly explains that certain Sunday saints get only the IX-ode incipit following the Italian sequence, whereas Greek reference canons generally present I,VI,IX.
findings.limit: This is explicit local receiving calendar/rubric context, no named full Eucharistic celebrant book, first adoption, textual collation, decree of approval or uniform parish use.

support: piana-publisher2020.html, product description and Product JSON-LD
findings.assertion: Primary co-publisher lists a 2020 Greek/Italian coedition with Piana, ISBN 9788897789796, same two reference sets/rubric explanation, 384 pages.
findings.limit: Retail catalogues list 368 pages; original 2020 volume/approval leaves not inspected. Supplemental source only; no extra annual state proposed.

findings.assertion: Official Athens Holy Trinity cathedral/parish programme posted 24 March 2026 schedules Presanctified 6–8 April, Vespers/Basil 9 and 11 April and Paschal Orthros/Divine Liturgy at midnight before 12 April. Official 16 May programme separately schedules Pentecost 31 May and Holy Spirit Monday 1 June.
findings.limit: Published intended local arrangements, not proof completed celebrations, receiving edition, liturgical performance language, Greek exarchate-wide practice or Roman 1950/1952 book reception. Proposed stage is a calendar/rubric programme component only.

findings.assertion: Official current pages describe Presanctified Wednesdays/Fridays 18:15; local Theotokos feast 22 August; annual dual Italo-Byzantine/Roman calendars. Typikon page gives monastic spirituality.
findings.limit: Pages are undated and identify no exact receiving service-book edition or adoption date. No new Grottaferrata stage proposed. Current circular/homily PDF requests returned 403; no contents inferred.

sources.title: Lajme / Notizie, January–April 2015
sources.inspection: Original PDF p. 25 (two-up printed pp. 48–49) directly inspected as raster 20 October 2026; named book and current Lungro use in right-hand printed p. 49.
sources.locus: Reports the 1968 first printed Arbëresh Chrysostom Liturgy (Tipografia Italo-Orientale S. sources.title: Il sogno di Dio sulla nostra Chiesa, pastoral letter 2018/2019
sources.inspection: Bishop Donato Oliverio’s pastoral PDF pp. 30–31 directly inspected as rasters 20 October 2026; other earlier inspection loci remain in prior record.
sources.locus: Reports the 1939 instruction on Greek books, the first inter-eparchial synod of 13–16 October 1940, and a decree of 13 October 1968 (citing Bollettino Ecclesiastico 1968, no. III, pp. 14–16) adopting Albanian in two editions, Greek with Albanian and Albanian with Italian.
sources.limitation: The retrospective says decreed adoption 13 October 1968, whereas Lajme 2023 gives decree publication 6 August 1968. Preserve both reports pending original Bollettino 3 (1968), 14–16. No exact Greek receiving edition is named.

sources.title: Imerologhion 2026, Eparchy of Lungro
sources.inspection: Original PDF pp. 3 (title), 60 (Pascha), 196 (Piana appendix credit) directly inspected as rasters 20 October 2026; whole text layer searched only as finding aid.
sources.locus: The annual calendar of Lungro, with proper appendices attributed to Piana, including the office for Blessed Josif Papamihali on 5 November.
sources.limitation: A search snippet had identified the whole volume as Piana's; the cover corrects this to Lungro, while the file keeps its discovery name. Whether the individual new propers are original compositions or translations, and their approval, are open.

versions.note: Its own Note per l’uso identifies the Roman Greek Anthologion 1967–1980 and the Italian Lipa Anthologhion 1999–2000 as reference books. The editors follow the Italian layout, with only ode IX indicated for certain saints on some Sundays, contrasting the generally I, VI, IX form of the Greek reference. This is source-described local calendrical/rubrical reception, not a collated textual descent, Eucharistic altar-book identity or universal local implementation.

versions.church_scope: Eparchy of Lungro (with the inter-eparchial commission)
versions.book_label: Liturgjia Hyjnore e atit tonë ndër shëjtrat Joan Hrysostomit
versions.date: Printing 1967 or 1968 reported; decree publication 6 August 1968 per 2023 retrospective; decreed adoption 13 October 1968 per 2018 pastoral; use explicitly attested 2015 and 2018
versions.note: Official Lungro sources identify the inter-eparchial Arbëresh Chrysostom Liturgy, Congregation approval and actual continued parish use. Lajme 2015 printed p. 49 explicitly names Liturgjia Hyjnore e atit tonë ndër shëjtrat Joan Hrysostomit (reported 1968, S. Nilo Grottaferrata) and says it remains used in Lungro Arbëresh parishes. The bishop’s 2018 pastoral PDF pp. 30–31 identifies Greek–Albanian and Albanian–Italian approved formats and says Albanian is commonly used in almost all its parishes. This meets received-service-book-language scope and is not blanket-deferred solely as a translation. Printing 1967 versus 1968, press and bilingual-format discrepancies remain unresolved until original title/approval leaves are inspected. Lajme 2023 p. 104 gives decree publication 6 August 1968; the 2018 pastoral p. 30 says adoption decreed 13 October 1968. These reports do not authorize a silently harmonized exact adoption day. No Piana, Grottaferrata or Albanian Catholic local reception is inferred.
versions.date_basis: Distinct source-reported publication/adoption/use dates are preserved; no numeric printing bound or invented reconciliation.
versions.source_title_status: Source-supplied bibliographic label; native title page not independently inspected unless stated

versions.church_scope: Eparchy of Lungro, with appendices credited to the Eparchy of Piana degli Albanesi
versions.book_label: Imerologhion 2026 with proper appendices attributed to Piana
versions.language: Italian for the Piana appendix propers; other parts as printed
versions.note: Original Lungro title and calendar inspected. The official 20 January 2026 announcement expressly says the eparchy has circulated this Ordo to regulate the year’s festive/daily Vespers, Orthros, Hours and Divine Liturgy. PDF p. 60 assigns Pascha 5 April 2026 and Chrysostom with proper hymns/readings; this is a concrete local operative calendar/rubric component, not a new Eucharistic recension. PDF pp. 196 and 199 credit Piana’s Liturgical Office for Italian propers, which does not make the whole volume Piana’s. Exact receiving Hieratikon, decree for the appended propers, first celebration and parish-wide compliance remain unproved.
